title: Vishal:
title_short: Vishal · How a Kiva Loan Works
headline: One farmer in Uganda, one $25 loan, six simple steps: where your money goes and how it comes back.
story: Kiva's CEO walks a forest path and explains a Kiva loan through one farmer in Uganda. A local partner shares the story. People pool $25 or $50. The partner lends it. The farmer grows the farm and repays. The money comes back, and you lend it again.
This one is the mechanics, told simply. Keep all six steps, in order, and make each one easy to see. It ends on the idea Kiva wants you to remember: the money keeps cycling and creating more impact.
do: Open on frame 1 with Vishal already saying “Imagine there's a farmer in Uganda”.
Show one short step label as each step lands. Six labels, in order.
Put the step labels at the top. Keep the lower third for captions.
Small name super after the hook: “Vishal Ghotge” / “CEO of Kiva”.
Cut the crew line and the first, repeated pass at step 2.
dont: No name plate, logo or fade at 0:00.
No emotion or borrower profile. This is the how-it-works video.
No “Awesome, that sounded great” or any crew talk.
No big lime captions. Brit's caption spec only.

Brit's CEO-series style: about 25% smaller than the first round, inside the lower third, Kiva green #2AA967, a little less blur behind, a little more space between letters, soft (not hard) shadow edge. Post Grotesk if available. Max 2 lines. Not #EDF4F1 on #223829.
Two files: H.264 MP4 1920×1080 (16:9) and 1080×1920 (9:16), about 16 Mbps. Same cut, same captions, re-framed.
checklist: His name is Vishal Ghotge (G-H-O-T-G-E). The super reads “Vishal Ghotge” / “CEO of Kiva”. Never the transcript's “Kodke”.
The word “investment” is nowhere on screen.
Captions match his words exactly. No dropped words. Lines break at natural phrases.
Captions are Kiva green #2AA967, about 25% smaller, low, a little less blur, a little more letter spacing. Not #EDF4F1 on #223829.
No name super, logo or fade at 0:00. The new green K logo sits in a top corner, never on frame 1.
End card reads exactly “Give a little. Change a lot.” plus kiva.org.
Both versions exported: 16:9 and 9:16. Nothing important is cut off in the 9:16 crop.
The six step labels are in order and none says “invest”.

decisions.t: No visual reference on this shoot
decisions.b: Production Planning has no reference for the Seattle shoot. Nick has to pick one.

At WAV 01:05 he says “to invest in their business”. Kiva's legal rule bans “investment” on screen. This plan keeps his words in the captions and keeps “invest” out of the labels. Kiva's own How-Kiva-Works reel caption uses “invests in people”. Brit should confirm, or the editor cuts to “use this money … in their farm”.
Editor: Bleron or Qendrim? The board says Bleron; the brief doc on this item is addressed to Qendrim. Confirm Bleron.

client_note: Why this matters here: Kiva checks every word on screen. On this one the risk is the step labels: short, exact and never “investment”.
